32.subject: Botany
32.text: Cork cambium results in the formation of cork which becomes impermeable to water due to the accumulation of
32.sol: Cork cambium is a secondary lateral meristem that may arise from permanent living cells of hypodermis or outer cortex. It is composed of a single layer of meristematic cells. Its cells divide tangentially and periclinally towards the outer face and produce cork cells. These cells are compactly arranged and have thin cellulose walls in the beginning. As they mature there is a gradual loss of living matter and cells get elongated radially, vertically or tangentially. The cell walls become thick because of development

options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
217.sol: Biotic or ecological succession is the formation of a series of biotic communities at the same site over a period of time one after the other, till a stable climax community develops over the area. It occurs generally in bare areas. Primary succession takes place on a biological sterile soilless primary barren area. Secondary succession takes place in a recently denuded area which still contains a lot of organic debris, remains and propagules of previous living organisms. The area has become bared due to destructio

275.text: Assertion : The two cotyledons in the seed are often referred to as the embryonic leaves. Reason : The embryo contains radicle and plumule.
options: If both the assertion and reason are true and reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but assertion is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
If the assertion is true but the reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
275.sol: In a typical angiospermic plant, cotyledons in the seed are the embryonic leaves. The radicle of the embryo upon the seed germination produces the root system and the plumule produces the shoot system. The radicle and plumule are contained in the embryo.

1996.text: Assertion : Insulin is antagonistic to glucagon. Reason : It is an anabolic hormone.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
1996.sol: Glucagon stimulates the liver to convert stored glycogen into glucose. Glucagon is also called an "anti-insulin" hormone. Insulin is antagonistic to glucagon. Insulin converts glucose into glycogen in the liver and muscles. It promotes protein synthesis in tissue from amino acids.Insulin reduces catabolism of proteins. It is an anabolic hormone. It increase the synthesis of fat in the adipose tissue from fatty acids. Insulin reduces the breakdown and oxidation of fat.

Assertion A : Haloalkanes react with KCN to form alkyl cyanides as a main product while with AgCN form isocyanide as the main product. Reason R : KCN and AgCN both are highly ionic compounds. In the light of the above statement, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: A is correct but R is not correct
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is not correct but R is correct
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
30243.sol: KCN is ionic in nature and provides cyanide ions in solution. Although both carbon and nitrogen atoms are in a position to donate electron pairs, the attack takes place mainly through carbon atom and not through nitrogen atom since C - C bond is more stable than C - N bond. Involved reaction is shown below: R - X → Substitution reaction R - CN + KX Alkyl halide Cyanide Reaction of alkyl halide with AgCN AgCN is mainly covalent in nature. Here only nitrogen is free to donate electron pairs,hence it forms isocyanide

30392.text: An optically active alkyl bromide C₄ H₉ Br, reacts with ethanolic KOH to form major compound [A] which reacts with bromine to give compound [B]. One molecule of water adds to compound [C] on warming with mercuric sulphate and dilute sulphuric acid at 333 K to form compound [D]. The functional group in compound D will be confirmed by :
30392.sol: The optically active alkyl bromide C ₄ H ₉ Br is 2 -bromobutane, CH ₃ CH ( Br ) CH ₂ CH ₃ . Reaction with ethanolic KOH undergoes dehydrohalogenation to form but- 2 -ene as the major product [A] (Zaitsev's rule). But- 2 -ene [A] reacts with Br ₂ to form 2,3 -dibromobutane [B], CH ₃ CH ( Br ) CH ( Br ) CH ₃ . Compound [B] undergoes double dehydrohalogenation with ethanolic KOH and NaNH ₂ to give but- 2 -yne [C], CH ₃ C CCH ₃ . Hydration of but- 2 -yne [C] with HgSO ₄ and dilute H ₂ SO ₄ yields butan- 2 -one [D], CH

31412.text: Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R : Assertion (A) : BeCl 2 and MgCl 2 produce characteristic flame Reason (R) : The excitation energy is high in BeCl 2 and MgCl 2 In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
Both ( A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
31412.sol: In Be   and   Mg , the electrons are strongly bound. The energy required to excite these electrons is very high. Therefore, when the electron reverts back to its original position, the energy released does not fall in the visible region. Hence, no colour in the flame is seen.

79374.subject: Botany
79374.text: Cortex is the region found between:
79374.sol: Cortex is the region present between epidermis and stele. The term cortex refers to the outermost layer of cells on a plant's stem or root. The cortex has the ability to transport nutrients into the core of the root. It uses diffusion to achieve transport. It also stores nutrients in the form of starch. The cortex acts as a protective covering on plant and is often waterproof. Depending on the type of plant, the cortex can also store carbohydrates, tannins, essential oils, and resins.

79599.subject: Botany
79599.text: Which one of the following fungi contains hallucinogens?
79599.sol: Amanita muscaria is a species of poisonous mushroom. It contains a psychoactive compound known as muscimol having hallucinogenic properties. Morchella is edible fungi. Neurospora is used in genetics studies. Ustilago causes smut diseases in plants.

79994.subject: Botany
79994.text: Which of the following protects nitrogenase inside the root nodule of a leguminous plant?
79994.sol: L e g -Haemoglobin is a pink O ₂ scavanger- pigment present in root nodules of leguminous plants. It helps in protection of Nitrogenase from the O ₂ , as it is O ₂ -sensitive enzyme.

80195.subject: Botany
80195.text: Electrons from excited chlorophyll molecule of photosystem-II are accepted first by
80195.sol: Photosystem-II is a photosynthetic pigment system alongwith some electron carriers that is located in the apressed part of grana thylakoids. Photocentre has a dimer of special chlorophyll-a molecules called P ₆₈₀ . P ₆₈₀ of photosystem-II absorbs light energy, gets excited and transfers its electrons to electron acceptor molecule phaeophytin. Phaeophytin on accepting electrons become strong reducing agent. It donates, its electrons to downstream component of ETC, i e , quinone, cyt- b cyt- f complex, plastocyanin.

80380.subject: Botany
80380.text: Selaginella and Salvinia are considered to represent a significant step towards evolution of seed habit because
options: female gametophyte is free and gets dispersed like seeds
magaspores possess endosperm and embryo surrounded by seed coat
embryo develops in female gametophyte which is retained on parent sporophyte
80380.sol: Selaginella and Salvinia are heterosporous as they produce two kinds of spores-mirco (small) spores and macro (large) spores. The microspores and megaspores germinate and give rise to male and female gametophyte, respectively. The female gametophyte in these plants are retained on the parent sporophytes for variable periods. The development of the zygotes into young embryos takes place within the female gametophytes. This event is the precursor to the seed habit considered to an important step in evolution.

80950.subject: Chemistry
80950.text: Which one of following statements is not correct of sigma- and Pi - bonds formed between two carbon atoms?
options: Sigma-bond is stronger than a pibond
Bond energies of sigma-and pi-bonds are of the order of 264 ~kJ / mol and 347 ~kJ / mol , respectively
Free rotation of atoms about a sigmabond is allowed but not in case of a pi-bond
Sigma bond determines the direction between carbon atoms but a pi-bond has no primary effect in the regard
80950.sol: Bond energies of sigma and pi-bonds are of the order of 264 ~kJ / mol and 347 ~kJ / mol respectively as bond energy of sigma bond is greater than pi bond. Related Theory A sigma bond is stronger because of the head to head overlapping, while a pi bond is weaker because of side to side overlapping. A sigma bond requires more energy to break than a pi bond does.

84109.subject: Zoology
84109.text: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding blood pressure?
options: 100 / 55 mmHg is considered an ideal blood pressure
190 / 110 mmHg may harm vital organs like brain and kidney
130 / 90 mmHg is considered high and requires treatment
84109.sol: Hypertension is the term for blood pressure that is higher than normal (120 / 80) . In this measurement, 120 ~mm Hg (millimeter) of mercury pressure) is the systolic, or pumping, pressure and 80 ~mm Hg is the diastolic, or resting pressure. If repeated checks of blood pressure 190 / 100 ~mm Hg ) of an individual is 140 / 90 (140 over 90) or higher, it shows hypertension. High blood pressure leads to heart diseases and also affects vital organs like brain and kidney.

84162.subject: Zoology
84162.text: Lungs does not collapse between breaths and some amount of air will always remain in the lungs which can never be expelled because,
options: There is a negative pressure in the lungs
There is a negative intrapleural pressure pulling at the lung walls
There is a positive intrapleural pressure
Pressure in the lungs is higher than the atmospheric pressure
84162.sol: The pressure within the pleural cavity is slightly less than that of atmospheric pressure and this is referred to as negative pressure. Hence, the lungs do not collapse between breaths and some air always remains in it. Even after the most forceful expiration, there will be sufficient volume of air in the lungs. This is called residual volume. It is about 1.2 litre in males and 1.1 litre in females.

84505.subject: Zoology
84505.text: Which one of the following is not a property of cancerous cells, whereas the remaining three are?
options: They compete with normal cells for vital nutrients
They do not remain confined in the area of formation
They divide in an uncontrolled manner
84505.sol: Contact inhibition is the natural process of arresting cell growth when two or more cells come in contract with each other. It is a property of normal cells. Cancer cells divide in uncontrolled manner and do not show contact inhibition.

84788.subject: Zoology
84788.text: The primitive prokaryotes responsible for the production of biogas from the dung of ruminant animals, include the:

Halophiles, thermoacidophiles and methanogens are archaebacteria. Methanogens are present in the rumen of cattle that is present in dung as well. It helps in production of methane gas that is a component of biogas.

101907.text: Assertion : When hot water is poured in a beaker of thick glass, the beaker cracks. Reason : Outer surface of the beaker expands suddenly.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion

101907.sol: When we pour hot water in beaker, the inner surface of the glass expands on heating. But heat from inside does not reach quickly the outer surface of the glass, because glass is a bad conductor of heat. Hence, the outer surface does not expand and the glass cracks.

104343.subject: Physics
104343.text: A piece of blue glass heated to a high temperature and a piece of red glass at room temperature are taken inside a dimly-lit room. Then,

Further away from the apex, i.e., more proximal to the phase of elon
124674.sol: The cells proximal to the meristematic zone represent the phase of elongation. Increased vacuolation, cell enlargement and new cell wall deposition are the characteristics of the cells in this phase. . Further away from the apex, i.e., more proximal to the phase of elongation, lies the portion of axis which is undergoing the phase of maturation. The cells of this zone, attain their maximal size in terms of wall thickening and protoplasmic modifications.

125171.subject: Botany

125171.sol: In glycolysis, ATP is utilized at two specific steps. The first ATP is consumed when glucose is phosphorylated to form glucose-6-phosphate. The second ATP is consumed when fructose-6-phosphate is phosphorylated to form fructose-1,6-bisphosphate. Therefore, the direct products of these two ATP-consuming reactions are glucose-6-phosphate and fructose-1,6-bisphosphate. Fructose-6-phosphate is a substrate, not a product, of the second ATP-consuming step. 3-phosphoglyceric acid and pyruvic acid are products of ATP-gener

130400.text: Steps of Muscle Contraction Description A. ATP Binding 1. Myosin head binds to actin filament, forming a cross-bridge B. Cross-Bridge Formation 2. Myosin head pivots, pulling the actin filament towards the center of the sarcomere C. Power Stroke 3 .ATP binds to the myosin head, causing it to detach from the actin filament D. 130400.sol: ATP Binding: ATP binds to the myosin head, leading to its detachment from actin. Cross-Bridge Formation: Myosin head binds to actin, forming a cross-bridge. Power Stroke: The myosin head pivots, pulling the actin filament towards the center of the sarcomere. Release of ADP and Pi: This release triggers the power stroke, allowing contraction.

The vasa efferentia leave the testis and open into epididymis located along the posterior surface of each testis. The epididymis leads to vas deferens that ascends to the abdomen and loops over the urinary bladder. It receives a duct from seminal vesicle and opens into urethra as the ejaculatory duct. These parts of the system along with a pair of the mammary glands are integrated structurally and functionally to support the processes of ovulation, fertilisation, pregnancy, birth and child care. 133620.sol: Interferon is a group of proteins that increases the resistance of cells to viral infection. Interferon also acts as cytokines and can enhance some immune responses. Three types of interferons have so far been discovered, alpha, beta and gamma, all of which have immune-modulating effects. Interferons are used in the treatment of cancer and autoimmune diseases.

(A) Fungus, (B) Clostridium butylicum, (C) Cyclosporin A, (D) Statins
133977.sol: Aspergillus niger is a fungus that produces citric acid, so (A) is Fungus. Butyric acid is produced by the bacterium Clostridium butylicum, so (B) is Clostridium butylicum. Monascus purpureus is a yeast that produces statins (used as blood-cholesterol lowering agents), so (C) is Statins. Trichoderma polysporum is a fungus that produces Cyclosporin A (used as an immunosuppressive agent), so (D) is Cyclosporin A. Therefore, the correct sequence is (A) Fungus, (B) Clostridium butylicum, (C) Statins, (D) Cyclosporin A.

If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
134030.sol: Queen is the only fertile female in beehive, having immensely developed ovaries. She lives for several successive years laying about 2000 or more eggs a day. The queen has a remarkable capacity of controlling the fertilisation of its eggs. A fertilised egg is laid in a worker or queen cell, while an unfertilised egg in a drone cell, the latter develops parthenogenetically. The queen mates only once in her life time. The sperms stored in her spermatheca fertilise her eggs as long as she lives.

6a1bb6bc107bf677676d9f21.subject: Physics
6a1bb6bc107bf677676d9f21.text: What is the magnitude of the component of the electric field parallel to an equipotential surface?
options: Equal to the net electric field
Equal to the perpendicular component of the field
Dependent on the local surface charge density
6a1bb6bc107bf677676d9f21.sol: By definition, the electric potential V is constant everywhere on an equipotential surface. The component of the electric field along any direction is given by E = - dV dr . For any displacement dr parallel to the equipotential surface, the change in potential dV = 0 . Therefore, the component of the electric field parallel to the equipotential surface is E_ = - 0 dr = 0 . This implies that the electric field is always perpendicular to the equipotential surface, and its parallel component is zero. Answer: Zero

96309.subject: Botany
96309.text: During meiosis, a microspore mother cell has 12 bivalents, the number of chromosomes in its pollen grains will be:
96309.sol: Meiosis is a reductional type of division where the chromosome numbers are halved in the daughter cells formed. During the meiotic division process, there is formation of bivalents which are paired homologous chromosomes. If cell has 12 bivalents, then the mother cell will have 24 chromosomes. Pollen grains are formed from each of the daughter cell formed after a complete meiotic process of a microspore mother cell. Thus, the chromosomes in pollen grain will be half of the mother cell which is 12.

309489.text: Consider the dehydration of 1-methylcyclohexanol in the presence of concentrated H ₂ SO ₄ . What is the correct order of the relative yields of the following products? (I) (II) (III)

304754.subject: Physics
304754.text: It is possible for an object to have
options: a nonzero acceleration without possessing a varying velocity
a nonzero acceleration without possessing a varying speed
a varying speed without possessing a varying velocity
a varying velocity without possessing a varying speed
304754.sol: Velocity is a vector quantity which has both magnitude (speed) and direction. Acceleration is defined as the rate of change of velocity. If the velocity is constant, the acceleration must be zero. Thus, an object cannot have a nonzero acceleration without a varying velocity. If an object moves with a constant speed but changes its direction of motion (for example, in uniform circular motion), its velocity is varying. How much of the energy emitted per second by the inner surface of B falls back onto this surface itself?

306506.text: Within a room containing air, heat can transfer from one location to another
306506.sol: Heat transfer in a room containing air can occur through all three modes: conduction, convection, and radiation. Conduction takes place due to the collision of air molecules, though it is a slow process since air is a poor conductor. Convection occurs as heated air becomes less dense and rises, creating convection currents that transfer heat effectively. 6a7a1ff805c5c1fbeaa2c73e.sol: The average translational kinetic energy per molecule of any ideal gas depends only on its absolute temperature T and is given by the expression 3 2 k_B T , where k_B is the Boltzmann constant.
